A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NEG/NeurGrad study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and content can be matched across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original neuron-intervention, NEG-estimation, knowledge-attribution, and MCEval8K probing results, with additional analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds Tree-Probe evaluations, activation-based comparisons, and analyses of neuron interdependencies.

M1.justification: V3 adds Tree-Probe, a random-forest classifier using each neuron's highest-NEG answer-token index as a feature, alongside the existing polarity- and magnitude-based majority-vote probes. This introduces a substantive new probing procedure. NeurGrad's estimation formula and the two existing probes remain unchanged apart from terminology.

E1.justification: Both versions use MyriadLAMA and the same 22 MCEval8K tasks across six genres, with the same five-language multilingual coverage. The dataset table, task prompt templates, and 12-context PAWS scenario are retained. Changes to the tested model panel do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 compares skill probes with Rand and LM-Prob; v3 additionally evaluates Wang et al.'s activation-based probe on six tasks across four LLMs in Table 3. This supplies a substantive direct comparison with prior skill-neuron probing. CG, IG, and LPI remain comparators in the NEG-estimation or attribution evaluations.

E3.justification: The nine-model intervention panel becomes seven models: BERTwwm, Llama2-13B, pretrained Llama2 variants, and Phi3-mini are removed, while Llama3.2-3B, Llama3.1-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B are introduced. V3 also adds random-forest evaluation with 100 unrestricted-depth trees and controlled depth/tree-count sweeps. The retained dataset splits and intervention ranges remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds studies of neuron interdependency through forest-depth and tree-count variation, including a fixed-1024-feature hierarchy comparison in Appendix H.3 and a learned PAWS decision-tree example. The efficiency, contextual-robustness, and neuron-substitutability analyses largely match v2's Appendices H–I and are relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V3 Appendix B.3 changes 'means and variances' to 'means and confidence interval,' but Figure 12 still labels the displayed statistics as variances. No confidence level or interval-estimation procedure resolves this inconsistency. Neither version specifies repeated-run or seed counts, so a genuine change in uncertainty reporting cannot be established reliably.

E6.justification: V3 adds Tree-Probe results, averaging 0.817/0.832 for zero-/few-shot prompting in Figure 6, activation-baseline results, new-model results, and hierarchy findings. Shared per-task majority-vote results remain unchanged. Reported Llama2-70B CG/NeurGrad MAEs change from 5.9e-07/2.1e-09 in v2 Table 1 to 2.2e-04/5.9e-07 in v3 Table 2; LPI's MAE entries disappear.

T1.justification: V3 Section 4.3 explicitly identifies NEG with the output-coordinate partial derivative at the activation vector, whereas v2 Section 5.3 invokes local Taylor approximation to explain the fitted intervention slopes without that explicit identification. This is a limited formal-definition addition, not a new proof. The regression definition, probing objective, and layer/prompt generality equations are retained.

C1.justification: The central claims about global neuron linearity, NeurGrad, NEG-based skill representation, and MCEval8K remain. V3's abstract and introduction additionally emphasize neuron interdependency and list efficiency, robustness, and substitutability as contribution properties. Most of the latter properties were already established in v2's appendices, limiting the substantive claim expansion.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations linking gradient probes to undertrained complex knowledge and target-token-specific representation, plus interpretations of forest-depth preferences as skill-dependent neuron interdependencies. These substantially expand the interpretation beyond v2's model-size/knowledge-recall discussion. Existing contextual sensitivity and limitations concerning single-token probing and untested skill-level editing remain.

D1.justification: Appendix G.2 newly documents Tree-Probe's token-index features, scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier implementation, defaults, and example-tree configuration; Sections 6.4 and H.3 specify parameter sweeps. Model identifiers and architecture information are revised. The anonymous release link is replaced by named GitHub code and Hugging Face dataset locations, adding substantial reproducibility and access information.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations to Oba et al., Sundararajan et al., Heath et al., Pedregosa et al., and the Llama3 and Qwen reports, while removing the Phi3 report. It adds focused positioning against activation-based probing but retains the broader related-work framework. Several other reference edits merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and much of the main text are extensively rewritten. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 7; skill-probing material is consolidated into Section 5; and substantial appendix interpretation and properties material moves into Sections 5.5–6. Probe terminology and explanatory organization are revised throughout.

P2.justification: V3 adds decision-tree and forest-sensitivity figures, expands the probing radar plots and comparison tables, combines linearity and polarity statistics, and redesigns model-distribution displays. Existing appendix plots and tables are extensively relocated, resized, and grouped, including placing both per-task accuracy tables on one page.

improvement.justification: The added activation baseline in Table 3 and documented Tree-Probe analyses in Appendices G–H improve comparative evidence and reproducibility. These benefits are tempered by large differences in probe neuron counts, which complicate interpreting the new accuracy advantage, and inconsistent confidence-interval/variance labeling in Appendix B.3 and Figure 12. The net improvement is useful but limited.
